t.1.15.2: O gods, what is the means for slaying that lord of the rākṣasas, by adopting which I may strike down that thorn of the sages?
t.1.15.1: Then Nārāyaṇa Viṣṇu, thus appointed by the foremost of the gods, though he already knew all, spoke gentle words to the gods.
t.1.15.3: Thus addressed, all the gods replied to the imperishable Viṣṇu: "Assuming a human body, slay Rāvaṇa in battle."
t.1.15.5: Well pleased, the Lord granted that rākṣasa a boon: there would be no fear for him from beings of many kinds, except from a man.
t.1.15.4: For he, O subduer of foes, practised fierce austerity for a long time, and with him Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, honoured by the worlds, became pleased.
t.1.15.7: Having heard these words of the gods, the self-possessed Viṣṇu then chose King Daśaratha as his father.
t.1.15.6: Long ago, at the granting of the boon, men were held in contempt by him; therefore, O scorcher of foes, his death is foreseen to come from men.
t.1.15.8: At that time that sonless king of great splendour, the slayer of foes, desiring a son, performed the sacrifice for obtaining sons.
t.1.15.9: Then indeed, from the fire of the sacrificer, there appeared a great being of incomparable splendour, of great valour and great strength.
t.1.15.10: It was dark, clad in red garments, red-mouthed, with a voice like the boom of a kettledrum, its body hair, beard and splendid locks glossy like a lion's mane.
t.1.15.11: It was endowed with auspicious marks and adorned with divine ornaments; towering as high as a mountain peak, it had the prowess of a proud tiger.
t.1.15.12: Its form was like the sun, resembling the flame of a blazing fire, and it bore a vessel made of refined gold, covered with a silver lid.
t.1.15.13: Holding in his own arms, as though it were a beloved wife, a large vessel filled with divine pāyasa, a vessel that seemed fashioned of magic.
t.1.15.14: Having looked at him, he spoke these words to King Daśaratha: "Know me, O king, to be a being sent by Prajāpati, who has come here."
t.1.15.15: Then, after that, the king replied with joined palms: "O blessed one, may there be welcome to you! What shall I do for you?"
t.1.15.16: Then the being sent by Prajāpati spoke these words once more: "O king, this has been obtained by you today, as you were worshipping the gods."
t.1.15.17: O tiger among men, take this pāyasa prepared by the gods, which bestows offspring, brings good fortune and increases health.
t.1.15.18: Give this to your worthy wives, saying, 'Eat.' In them, O king, you will obtain the sons for whose sake you are performing this sacrifice.
t.1.15.20: And having saluted that wondrous being, pleasing to behold, he, filled with supreme joy, walked reverently around it, keeping it on his right.
t.1.15.21: Then Daśaratha, having received the pāyasa made by the gods, became supremely delighted, like a penniless man who has obtained wealth.
t.1.15.19: Saying “So be it,” the delighted king reverently received upon his head that golden vessel, filled with divine food and given by the gods.
t.1.15.22: Then that being of wondrous appearance, supremely radiant, having accomplished that task, vanished right there.
t.1.15.24: As soon as he entered the inner apartments, he said this to Kausalyā: "Accept this rice-pudding, which brings a son for yourself."
t.1.15.23: Upon his announcement, his inner palace shone forth as if woven with rays of joy, like the sky shining with the beams of the lovely autumn moon.
t.1.15.25: Then the lord of men gave half of the pāyasa to Kausalyā, and the ruler of men also gave half of the remaining half to Sumitrā.
t.1.15.27: After reflecting, the lord of the earth gave to Sumitrā once again. Thus the king gave the pāyasa separately to each of his wives.
t.1.15.26: To Kaikeyī he gave half of what remained, for the sake of obtaining a son, and he then bestowed the last remaining half of the nectar-like pāyasa.
t.1.15.28: Having received this milk-rice, all those excellent wives of the lord of men, their hearts uplifted with great joy, regarded it as an honour.
